newsitem.title: FRANCE: UAP takes 7.59 billion francs in charges.
newsitem.headline: UAP takes 7.59 billion francs in charges.

text.p: French insurer UAP took 7.59 billion francs ($1.3 billion) in exceptionals as part of a drive to clean up its books ahead of its merger with Axa, Axa-UAP announced on Wednesday in a statement.
The exceptionals drove UAP into a 1996 net attributable loss of 6.45 billion francs. The previous year it had a net attributable loss of 2.1 billion francs.
Net profit for 1996 before exceptionals was 1.14 billion francs.

The exceptionals involved 3.84 billion francs for the deconsolidation of French bank BNP in UAP's accounts and a change in the investment horizon of some real estate companies -- Soffim, Sofapi and Sofinad -- which led to the disappearance of deferred tax credits.

Revaluation of some asset and liability items in life and property and casualty insurance companies in France, property and casualty insurance in Italy and of its banking unit Banque Worms accounted for a further 3.74 billion francs in provisions.
